investigations.name: draft-to-living-cell
investigations.title: From Draft to Living Cell
investigations.question:
Is a cellular interface simultaneously a modeling choice — a decision about which
ports matter, what units they carry, how a process couples to the rest of the cell — and a
testable biological hypothesis about which interactions actually govern a cell's fate? And
does treating composition as an ongoing practice — connect two interfaces where their
assumptions hold, cut the model open at the interface when those assumptions fail, coarse-grain
a resolved network back into a lumped exchange when organization re-emerges — let the same
cellular specification hold together across environment coupling, cell-cell coupling,
molecular mechanism, nested complementarity, autopoietic closure, growth, division, and the
harder transitions of development and evolution, while tracking viability bounds as the
locus of minimal agency throughout?
investigations.hypothesis:
Every recurring composition pattern in the cellular-interface paper — the typed
contract, environment coupling, cell-cell coupling, the disintegration/grain-swap that cuts
the model open at the interface, the molecular mechanism, nested complementarity, autopoietic
closure, growth-driven division, and the developmental/evolutionary rewrite — can be authored
as an inert draft (typed, unit-bearing ports + a structural contract, with no dynamics) and
then *compiled* — by installing one conforming mechanism per draft — into an executable that
preserves the paper's interface exactly and produces genuine dynamics. Across the 9 studies,
the interface is the site where ordinary chemical dynamics becomes a self-maintaining,
viability-bounded agent, and composition — connecting, cutting open, coarse-graining — is how
that boundary is built, tested, and maintained.

investigations.name: the-cellular-interface-multicellular
investigations.title: The Cellular Interface, Multicellular
investigations.question:
The companion investigation `draft-to-living-cell` specified the paper's nine
interface-composition patterns and ran them with toy-real, lumped mechanisms (ODEs, scripted
events, 1-D or 9-cell grids). This investigation asks whether the same patterns hold when the
environment is not a lumped store but a real 2D spatial field, and the cell is not a scalar
state bundle but a Cellular Potts Model (CPM) agent with genuine shape, footprint, and
motion. Concretely: does the Fig 5 sense/act loop survive being realized as a real CPM cell
(viva-cpm) sitting in a spatio-flux diffusing nutrient field, running dynamic flux-balance
analysis at its own footprint, growing, and secreting a metabolic byproduct back into the
field it depends on — composed from two independently-developed simulation frameworks through
one typed coupling interface (`CpmCellField`)?
investigations.hypothesis:
The paper's interface-composition patterns are not artifacts of the lumped,
low-dimensional mechanisms `draft-to-living-cell` used to demonstrate them — they hold when
the cell and its environment are realized in real 2D spatial frameworks built and validated
independently of this codebase (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes). One typed coupling process per pattern
(starting with `CpmCellField`, this investigation's flagship) is enough to compose those
frameworks without either one knowing about the other, and the resulting dynamics — nutrient
depletion, biomass growth, byproduct secretion and diffusion — are genuine simulation output,
not scripted. Across future increments, every one of the nine `draft-to-living-cell` studies
is expected to have a spatial counterpart; several are built and run so far (the flagship
cell-environment coupling, cell-cell coupling, disintegration, and growth-and-division), with
the rest planned or in progress.
